---
title: "Getting Started"
---

Both packages come from PyPI, `pip install estimint mintstate` brings in the pair, and one
district then goes from a measured prevalence, through the EIR inversion, to a prevalence
trajectory, in a single call to `run_scenarios`. Python 3.12 is the minimum. `stateMINT` is published on PyPI
under the distribution name `mintstate`, so the name in the install command is not the name in
the import. Both go into a virtual environment rather than the single shared library R keeps.
The emulator's weights are fetched on first use. They are cached under `~/.cache/huggingface`
rather than shipped in the wheel, which makes the first `run_scenarios` of a new install slower
than every call that follows it. Please see [Python for Malaria
Modellers](../01-python/index.qmd) if virtual environments are new.
